question: For the order-recorded city with the highest 2025 cancellation rate among cities with at least 50,000 orders, compare its cancellation rate and average Delivered-order delivery time with the overall 2025 figures. Can these figures establish that slower delivery caused cancellations?

action.query:
WITH order_facts AS (
  SELECT
    b.ORDER_ID,
    b.CITY,
    f.IS_CANCELLED,
    f.IS_DELIVERED,
    f.DELIVERED_TIME_MIN
  FROM ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_BASE b
  LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_FULFILLMENT f
    ON b.ORDER_ID = f.ORDER_ID
  WHERE b.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01'
    AND b.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01'
), city_stats AS (
  SELECT
    CITY,
    COUNT(*) AS ORDER_COUNT,
    COUNT_IF(IS_CANCELLED) AS CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT,
    COUNT_IF(IS_CANCELLED) / COUNT(*)::FLOAT AS CANCELLATION_RATE,
    COUNT_IF(IS_DELIVERED) AS DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT,
    AVG(IFF(IS_DELIVERED, DELIVERED_TIME_MIN, NULL)) AS AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN
  FROM order_facts
  GROUP BY CITY
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50000
), highest_rate_cities AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM city_stats
  QUALIFY RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CANCELLATION_RATE DESC) = 1
), overall_stats AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS ORDER_COUNT,
    COUNT_IF(IS_CANCELLED) AS CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT,
    COUNT_IF(IS_CANCELLED) / COUNT(*)::FLOAT AS CANCELLATION_RATE,
    COUNT_IF(IS_DELIVERED) AS DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT,
    AVG(IFF(IS_DELIVERED, DELIVERED_TIME_MIN, NULL)) AS AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN
  FROM order_facts
)
SELECT
  'HIGHEST_RATE_CITY' AS POPULATION,
  CITY,
  ORDER_COUNT,
  CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT,
  CANCELLATION_RATE,
  DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT,
  AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN
FROM highest_rate_cities
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'OVERALL_2025' AS POPULATION,
  'Overall' AS CITY,
  ORDER_COUNT,
  CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT,
  CANCELLATION_RATE,
  DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT,
  AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN
FROM overall_stats
ORDER BY POPULATION, CITY
action.metrics: 2025 recorded-order cancellation rate (cancelled orders / all recorded orders); average delivery time in minutes among delivered orders only
action.group_by: highest-cancellation-rate city among cities with at least 50,000 2025 recorded orders, plus all 2025 recorded orders overall

action.query: SELECT IFF(GROUPING(b.CITY) = 1, 'OVERALL_2025', 'HIGHEST_RATE_CITY') AS POPULATION, IFF(GROUPING(b.CITY) = 1, 'Overall', b.CITY) AS CITY, COUNT(*) AS ORDER_COUNT, COALESCE(COUNT_IF(f.IS_CANCELLED), 0) AS CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT, COALESCE(COUNT_IF(f.IS_CANCELLED), 0) / COUNT(*)::FLOAT AS CANCELLATION_RATE, COUNT_IF(f.IS_DELIVERED) AS DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT, AVG(IFF(f.IS_DELIVERED, f.DELIVERED_TIME_MIN, NULL)) AS AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN FROM ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_BASE b LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_FULFILLMENT f ON b.ORDER_ID = f.ORDER_ID WHERE b.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND b.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((b.CITY), ()) QUALIFY GROUPING(b.CITY) = 1 OR (COUNT(*) >= 50000 AND RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY GROUPING(b.CITY) ORDER BY COALESCE(COUNT_IF(f.IS_CANCELLED), 0) / COUNT(*)::FLOAT DESC) = 1) ORDER BY POPULATION, CITY
action.metrics: 2025 recorded-order cancellation rate (cancelled orders / all recorded orders); average delivery time in minutes among delivered orders only
action.group_by: Highest-rate recorded-order city with at least 50,000 2025 orders and overall 2025 recorded orders

action.query: SELECT b.CITY, COUNT(*) AS ORDER_COUNT, COUNT_IF(f.IS_CANCELLED) AS CANCELLED_ORDER_COUNT, COUNT_IF(f.IS_CANCELLED) / COUNT(*)::FLOAT AS CANCELLATION_RATE, COUNT_IF(f.IS_DELIVERED) AS DELIVERED_ORDER_COUNT, AVG(IFF(f.IS_DELIVERED, f.DELIVERED_TIME_MIN, NULL)) AS AVG_DELIVERED_ORDER_DELIVERY_TIME_MIN FROM ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_BASE b LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_FULFILLMENT f ON b.ORDER_ID = f.ORDER_ID WHERE b.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND b.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY b.CITY HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50000 ORDER BY CANCELLATION_RATE DESC LIMIT 1
action.metrics: 2025 recorded-order cancellation rate (cancelled / all orders); average delivery time in minutes among delivered orders
action.group_by: City; cities with at least 50,000 2025 recorded orders; top cancellation rate

action.metrics: Cancellation rate = cancelled orders / all recorded orders; average delivery time = mean delivered-order delivery time, in minutes.
action.answer: Using 2025 recorded orders (ORDER_DATE from 2025-01-01 up to but not including 2026-01-01), Hyderabad had the highest cancellation rate among cities with at least 50,000 orders: 19,236 of 319,122 orders were cancelled, a 0.060278 rate (6.027789%). Its average delivery time among 291,876 delivered orders was 31.096716 minutes. Overall, 261,456 of 4,359,773 orders were cancelled, a 0.059970 rate (5.997009%); average delivery time among 3,989,077 delivered orders was 31.074379 minutes. Hyderabad was higher by 0.030779 percentage points in cancellation rate and 0.022336 minutes in delivered-order average delivery time. These figures do not establish that slower delivery caused cancellations: they are descriptive comparisons, and delivery-time averages include delivered orders only, not cancelled orders.
